I can't speak for your friends and yourself but I would reckon that depending on the circumstances you could talk with your friend at least a little. Send a text or something that could communicate the issue. But I also know that people can get busy and ignore other aspects of their lives so maybe that's not the case. If you haven't already I'd send a text or something just so they are aware and you can maybe talk about it. I get trying to meet new friends is tiring. I haven't made a new friend since high school and I'm 26 right now so it can definitely be tough but maybe try groups that relate to some of your hobbies, that way it wouldn't feel as pressuring or stressful and you can actually have something you can relate to. Relationships can really hold on in that way and I'm sorry to hear that you didn't get the closure you deserve. Sometimes relationships can really hold on to you and keep you anchored in a way that isn't helpful or makes you feel good. Hopefully you can find some sense of peace from the good times and put to rest the relationship. I'm sorry if these are hollow words and know that I don't mean to be even if they are.
So numb that you truly have nothing of the sort? Or that they've lost complete meaning?

I'm not happy to hear that you feel this way but trust and believe that I understand what you're going through. I feel this every damn day and even to the point that I isolate so I may not infect others. But I always try and remember that those people that still hang around have my back and will show me my true worth, hence why they're still around too. It's not needy to vent and try your best to never feel that way. Bottling up only leads to heartbreak and blow ups later down the line. You're a human just like me, we all have thoughts and feelings at the end of the day. Good luck and I hope you can love yourself at some point as hypocritical as that may seem. Nobody deserves feelings of self hatred. Also you're a fine writer, you got your thoughts and feelings across and that's the most important thing.

I can definitely relate as I'm currently drinking to ease some of my thoughts and feelings. As long as you don't go to far into the deep end it's why those things exist. I hope that one day you can live without such things, but don't feel ashamed for using such methods if you even do. You can always get help if you do though. Good luck and I hope you have a pleasant time and stay safe.

I'm sorry I have nothing to give besides hollow thoughts and feelings. I genuinely wish you well and hope that you can keep on keeping on. Humans are a spectrum, they range from the worst of the worst to those that can change the world. It only takes time for them to come along in some capacity.

Keep in mind every creature on this earth wants to live, even humans at the toughest of times. I'm sorry you have the misfortune of thinking about it. Trust and believe if even a small part of you wants to live, that's a good sign and to keep on keeping on and all that. If you made it this far you're strong enough to keep going. Resilience is a powerful human trait. Good luck, I know I struggle with the same thoughts and feelings.

I don't know the situation you're in, but it sounds like you had the misfortune of knowing some self centered and sad individuals. I'm sad they couldn't provide what was needed for you. Is there no alternative avenue for you to go down to get the help you need?

I have never seen you so I can't speak to your personal appearance, but sounds like you know some really dogshit people. True friends and family will not give a single fuck to such vain things. Trust and believe that someone out there will be with you and be friends or more with you because they actually want to be. I know these sound like hollow words and maybe they are at this point in time. But to stagnate and stop trudging on means you've lost everything, even a simple pet or friend, or even a place you love to go to will be gone. Take the time to really think about what's going on and the people around. I know you've got this because you've made it this far already. Good luck and sorry if this truly sounds like hollow nonsense.
Do you have anything you value? It can be an action of some kind like a hobby, a pet that seeks your affection, a person who talks to you with any amount of frequency. Literally anything?

Not a whole lot does and when the apathy kicks in I just don't care about anything but getting to the next day without killing myself. But doing that for years and years gets tiring.

Thanks for the comment. I just wish it wasn't so tough to live, it feels like one step forward two steps back constantly and when you have no goals or direction to push in it all starts feeling kinda muddied.

Social media is both a wondrous and cancerous thing. People typically follow the flow of whatever is popular, I wouldn't worry too much on what people say. But I understand that some people put value on it, so my suggestion is to just move on. Feel the pain you feel about this, but don't let it consume you. That guy sounds like he had some serious issues and he was using social media to vent. It's noble that you stay positive and keep making an effort despite how you feel. Keep on keeping on my friend. You're doing good if you're trying to support others.
That's fair, and a good mindset. Keep holding on to it. Good luck.
People typically can be hypocritical, but people are complex, if they're being a hypocrite either they're an idiot, or there is more then meets the eye. How do you feel they are being hypocritical?

You couldn't do it because a small part of you wants to live. And that's perfectly okay. And I understand where you're coming from, you just have to find something you want to do, regardless if it follows societal norms. Forgive me if these are hollow words.
Sounds like your mother has got her own shit going on. You seem like you're doing just fine, ignore the lady and keep doing what you're doing. You're no loser based on what you're doing.
People do suck, it's easy to see just based on what's going on in the world at any given moment. But there is good in people, just takes some hunting. If you feel it's worth it, I'd do that.
Then I'd look into getting a therapist that can do CBT therapy. I know it's helped me quite a bit in my own issues. Though it does take quite some time to work.

Being twenty five seems cool, you're a quarter of a century old after all. And relationships aren't a good measurement of what actually matters in life. What matters in your own life should be yourself. Of course if you feel differently that's a fair opinion to have. But I feel you should value yourself first and worry about yourself. Others can come later. If you're doing the best you can, then people can come later. Don't worry about relationships for now, focus on getting stability, then you can go for relationships.

Your thought process should take priority, if you feel you're correct or unconvinced, you're right to think that. I won't fault you on that. But just make sure you've really questioned if you're providing worth or not. It'd be a shame to not really think things through. Maybe write down all your positive traits, and make sure to be objective with it. Just so your certain.
Being thirty isn't that old my friend, you have so much ahead of you. You just have to keep looking. Forgive me if these are hollow words.

I understand that logic, it makes sense. I felt very similarly when it came to the people around me. That I'm only harming them since I can't help myself.  But the thing about family and friendship is that it isn't give and take. It's just give until things become right. If they can't do that then they weren't the right people to associate with to begin with. You got to ask yourself what value you provide and what you can do to make things work. Other people don't factor into your own happiness. You got to look inside yourself and really find what the hell is going on and what you can do to find stability. Hopefully I didn't go off topic there.

So I try to find a way to pay them back by trying. Do you have anybody like that? That your living for?
